strings.name: Diane Greene
strings.role: VMware cofounder and former Google Cloud CEO
strings.summary: Diane Greene moved from naval architecture into computing, cofounding VMware and serving as its first CEO. She developed the commercial use of server virtualization through its EMC acquisition, IPO and leadership change. She later led Google Cloud and supported education and entrepreneurs. From 2020 to 2023 she was the MIT Corporation's first woman chair.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Cofounded VMware and developed its virtualization business, advancing data-center resource management and enterprise cloud computing.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Mechanical engineering BS, Vermont; naval architecture MS, MIT; computer science MS, Berkeley
strings.highlights.h1.title: Advancing server virtualization
strings.highlights.h1.text: With VMware's founding team, she built an enterprise infrastructure business and led its 2007 IPO.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Business and education leadership
strings.highlights.h2.text: She led Google Cloud and became the MIT Corporation's first woman chair, later chair emerita.
strings.timeline.t1.title: MIT chair term ends
strings.timeline.t1.text: Mark Gorenberg succeeded her as Corporation chair; she remained a life member.
strings.timeline.t2.title: MIT Corporation chair
strings.timeline.t2.text: She became the first woman to chair MIT's governing board.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Leaving Google Cloud
strings.timeline.t3.text: Thomas Kurian took over cloud leadership as she turned to investing, mentoring and philanthropy.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Leading Google's cloud business
strings.timeline.t4.text: After Google acquired Bebop, which she cofounded, she took full-time charge of cloud operations.
strings.timeline.t5.title: VMware leadership change
strings.timeline.t5.text: The board appointed Paul Maritz president and CEO, ending her decade of leadership.
strings.timeline.t6.title: VMware IPO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Following EMC's 2004 acquisition, she led VMware through its initial public offering.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Cofounding VMware
strings.timeline.t7.text: With Mendel Rosenblum and others, she founded the virtualization-software company and became CEO.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Computer science master's degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: She earned a second master's at Berkeley after earlier mechanical and naval engineering education.
